findings.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/resource_group.go:238` sets `resourceGroupSettings.Background = nil` for `BACKGROUND=NULL` / `BACKGROUND=()` (i.e., `len(opt.BackgroundOptions)==0`), but `pkg/ddl/resource_group.go:241` immediately overwrites it with `resourceGroupSettings.Background = &model.ResourceGroupBackgroundSettings{}`; loop is empty so the pointer can never stay nil.
First-parent behavior did not do this; it kept `Background=nil` for empty options and lazily allocated only when options exist: `git show 04608f499b41f5549ff6568222149cbe367b86fb^1:pkg/ddl/resource_group.go`.
Downstream effects: `pkg/ddl/resourcegroup/group.go:71` treats non-nil `options.Background` as present and always sends `group.BackgroundSettings`; `SHOW CREATE RESOURCE GROUP` always prints `BACKGROUND=...` when `Background!=nil` via `pkg/executor/show.go:1613` -> `pkg/meta/model/resource_group.go:126`.
findings.fix:
In `SetDirectResourceGroupSettings` (case `ast.ResourceGroupBackground`), make initialization conditional:
- `if len(opt.BackgroundOptions)==0 { resourceGroupSettings.Background = nil; return nil }`
- else `resourceGroupSettings.Background = &model.ResourceGroupBackgroundSettings{}` and apply options.
(Alternative: restore the old lazy-init in `SetDirectResourceGroupBackgroundOption` and remove the unconditional init.)
findings.impact: `ALTER RESOURCE GROUP default BACKGROUND=NULL/()` cannot truly unset background settings; TiDB persists an empty `Background` object and will still send a (zero-valued) `BackgroundSettings` message to the resource manager. This can cause inconsistent metadata presentation (`information_schema` shows NULL while `SHOW CREATE RESOURCE GROUP` still includes `BACKGROUND=()`), and risks semantic differences if the resource manager distinguishes “unset” (nil) vs “present-but-empty” background settings.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master` as of `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: `git show upstream/master:pkg/ddl/resource_group.go` still contains the same `len(opt.BackgroundOptions)==0` check followed by unconditional `resourceGroupSettings.Background = &model.ResourceGroupBackgroundSettings{}`.
findings.verify:
1) `ALTER RESOURCE GROUP default BACKGROUND=(TASK_TYPES='br,ddl', UTILIZATION_LIMIT=30)`; 2) `ALTER RESOURCE GROUP default BACKGROUND=NULL` (or `BACKGROUND=()`);
Expected after fix: `SHOW CREATE RESOURCE GROUP default` omits `BACKGROUND` (or otherwise reflects it as unset), and the resource-manager `ResourceGroup` no longer carries `BackgroundSettings` when cleared.
findings.what: `BACKGROUND=NULL` / `BACKGROUND=()` is not honored: DDL code always re-initializes `ResourceGroupSettings.Background` to a non-nil empty struct even when the AST indicates “clear background settings”.

subject: resource_control: support set resource limit for background tasks (#56020)
summary: Adds `BACKGROUND ... UTILIZATION_LIMIT` plumbing across parser/DDL/meta/infoschema, but introduces a High-severity DDL semantics bug: `BACKGROUND=NULL/()` cannot clear background settings to nil because the code unconditionally allocates an empty background settings struct; this persists on `upstream/master`.
